title: Tamsin and the Asset
premise: Juniper Galloway, a fixer for the Meridian Office — an embassy that exists on no map and answers to no flag — is repaid for a favor she has no memory of doing when a stranger named Tamsin arrives with proof that Juniper once saved her life. The debt comes with a demand: help Tamsin expose and destroy the Meridian training program that manufactured them both, before a Frankfurt market opening lets the program's architects launder their black budget into legitimacy. As Juniper follows rules that keep rewriting themselves, she must choose between loyalty to the only family she's ever known and the truth of what that family made her. In the end, Juniper burns the network from inside its own vault, loses her official existence entirely, and gains something she never had: a chosen family, with Tamsin, outside the walls.
about_author: August Joubert is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in cities that appear on no itineraries. They write thrillers about people whose loyalties are assigned rather than chosen.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A routine document burn in Vienna is interrupted by Tamsin, who returns a debt Juniper doesn't remember incurring — with a ledger entry proving Juniper saved her life seven years ago, an operation scrubbed from every record Juniper can access. The beat is disorientation: the first crack in Juniper's trust in her own history.

chapters.title: Rules, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Back at the Meridian Office, Juniper quietly investigates the ledger while executing a standard asset extraction that goes wrong in ways suggesting someone inside fed her false parameters. Her handler, Voss, reassures her with language that feels rehearsed. The emotional beat is creeping doubt wearing the mask of routine.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We learn what Tamsin survived: the Cradle, the training program that produced children like assets, and the Frankfurt scheme — a shell fund going live at market open in eleven days that will make its architects untouchable. She offers Juniper the choice plainly. The beat is a hand extended across a chasm.

chapters.title: The Family That Trains You
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Juniper tests Tamsin's story against her own muscle memory and finds gaps where memories should be — sedation gaps, exactly matching the ledger dates. Meanwhile Voss assigns Juniper to hunt the 'intruder,' making her the weapon aimed at her own ally. The beat is betrayal structured as employment.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hiding in Lisbon, Tamsin teaches Juniper how to read the Cradle's methods in their own reflexes; two guarded strangers begin trading small truths over bad coffee. Juniper realizes the office gave her colleagues but never kinship. The beat is found family taking root in fear.

chapters.title: Voss Makes a Call
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Inside Meridian, we see the machinery: Voss knows what Juniper is uncovering and reports upward to Director Hale, who orders Juniper brought in 'for recalibration' — the euphemism Tamsin barely escaped. Voss hesitates, revealing his own buried affection for Juniper. The beat is loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Recalibration
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Lured back under pretext, Juniper is captured and faces the recalibration suite — and learns the erased favor was real: she defied orders to pull Tamsin from a burning site, then chose to forget. Offered clean memory in exchange for surrendering Tamsin, she refuses. The beat is the past reclaimed as identity.

chapters.title: Two Days to Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin, aided by a guilt-wracked Voss, extracts Juniper in a violent, costly escape that burns Voss's career and nearly his life. With forty-eight hours to market open, they assemble the evidence chain: ledgers, the Cradle roster, Hale's signatures. The beat is desperation sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleave. In Frankfurt, they split — Tamsin penetrates the fund's launch event while Juniper breaches Meridian's archive vault to trigger the dead-man exposure. Hale corners Juniper among the servers and offers her old life back one final time; she answers by starting the burn. The climax is loyalty finally answering to truth.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, weeks later. The network is ash, Hale arrested through channels that officially never engaged, and Juniper's own records are gone — she no longer exists on paper, and finds the loss strangely light. She and Tamsin, plus a recovering Voss, share a table in a city with no operational value. The beat is belonging, unassigned at last.
